Commodity vol extremes: Chicago Fed, 'The Aftermath of the 2026 Oil Shock' (https://www.chicagofed.org/publications/chicago-fed-letter/2026/523); Vanguard, 'Oil shock complicates central bank outlooks' (https://corporate.vanguard.com/content/corporatesite/us/en/corp/vemo/oil-shock-complicates-central-bank-outlooks.html); WisdomTree, 'Gold and Silvers' Most Volatile Day' (https://www.wisdomtree.com/us/insights/blog/gold-and-silvers-most-volatile-day); Bold Precious Metals, 'Gold & Silver Market Volatility February 2026 Deep Dive' (https://www.boldpreciousmetals.com/news/gold-silver-market-volatility-february-2026). Mechanism: Frazzini & Pedersen (2014), 'Betting Against Beta', J. Financial Economics 111(1); Blitz & van Vliet (2007), 'The Volatility Effect', J. Portfolio Management.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_UUP_63
rationale: Structural/policy configuration, not a track-record claim -- I make no assertion about how the dollar, UUP, or any trend strategy has recently performed, and a sign rule takes both directions, so nothing here is a directional bet. THE MECHANISM. A trailing-sign trend rule has something to capture only if the asset's dominant driver is serially correlated. For a trade-weighted dollar index that driver is the relative short-rate path against the euro and the yen, which together are roughly 71% of the six-currency ICE USDX basket UUP's index is built on (EUR ~57.6%, JPY ~13.6% at the basket's fixed 1999 weights; UUP holds long USDX futures via the DB Long USD Currency Portfolio Index, not spot). That driver is serially correlated by institutional design rather than by accident: policy rates move in 25bp increments, at scheduled meetings roughly eight times a year, preceded by forward guidance and quarterly projection rounds, and every one of these committees explicitly values gradualism -- so a change in relative stance is a multi-meeting sequence, not a single repricing. The IMF's own decomposition of dollar dynamics finds the policy-divergence (neutral-rate) shock's effect on the dollar is both substantial and PERSISTENT, working mainly through future expected short rates. Persistence in the driver is the necessary condition for a sign rule; whether it survives into tradable serial correlation in the price is the empirical question the gates decide. WHY THE CURRENT CONFIGURATION MAKES THIS A TWO-SIDED TEST RATHER THAN A DISGUISED LONG-DOLLAR BET, which is the load-bearing part. All three major central banks have now exited the 2024-25 easing cycle, and they exited in different directions relative to the US: the ECB hiked its deposit rate 25bp to 2.25% on 2026-06-11 and held there in July; the BoJ hiked in June and held at 1.0% on 2026-07-31, its highest policy rate since September 1995, while warning core inflation will exceed its 2% target; and the Fed held the target range at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 for a fifth consecutive meeting. So the two heaviest basket counterparts are actively normalizing UPWARD into a frozen US front end -- the differential that dominates this index is compressing from a wide starting point. At the same time the US side's own next move has flipped sign inside the committee: three presidents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) dissented in favour of a HIKE, the first time since September 2016 that three policymakers dissented with a unified view of direction. Both legs of the differential are therefore live in both directions over the OOS window, which is exactly the sample a sign rule needs to be judged on honestly. WEAKNESSES, STATED FIRST RATHER THAN APPENDED. (1) The strongest prior is directly against this candidate and is specifically about exchange rates, specifically out-of-sample: Meese & Rogoff (1983) found no macro model -- interest-differential models included -- beats a random walk out of sample at horizons up to a year, and the subsequent literature has largely sustained that. If it holds, this dies at gate 1 and should. (2) Trend is the deadest family in this lab: tsmom_*, tsmom_gen_*, donchian_*, green_line_200d are all DEAD, and a currency ticker does not earn a lower bar for being new. (3) There is a real confound between trend and carry here. UUP is a long-USD FUTURES position, so its roll embeds the very short-rate differential the mechanism above rests on; under the forward-premium puzzle (Fama 1984) that roll has an average drift of its own, and a sign rule that is long the dollar most of the time would collect it while looking like trend. That confound is the second most likely reason this deserves to die, and neither this primitive nor the gates separate the two components. (4) UUP charges an expense ratio against a futures basket and tracks the DB index, not spot DXY. (5) The 2018-present OOS window contains both the favourable realisations (the 2018 and 2022 dollar runs, sustained moves a sign rule holds) and the worst ones (March 2020's spike-and-collapse, and extended range-bound chop, where a sign rule pays the whipsaw twice). PARAMETERS, DERIVED NOT SEARCHED. lookback=63 trading days is one quarter, which spans two FOMC meetings and two ECB monetary-policy Governing Council meetings (both ~8/yr) and one full quarterly projection round (the Fed's SEP, the ECB's staff projections) -- the shortest window over which a change in relative policy STANCE is observable as a sequence rather than as one meeting's surprise, and no longer than that. freq=W because a 63-day sign can flip on any session, and a monthly clock would act up to ~21 trading days late on a 63-day signal -- a third of the signal's own horizon -- whereas weekly keeps the execution lag under ~8% of it, at turnover a quarterly-horizon sign rule rarely triggers anyway. DISTINCTNESS. No graveyard.csv row is a single-ticker UUP strategy: the DEAD tsmom_*/tsmom_gen_* families trend all 15 UNIVERSE tickers as one ensemble, where UUP is 1/15 of the book and its own signal is netted against fourteen others, so a UUP-only trend has never been isolated. In this ledger the currency asset class is the least represented of the five -- UUP has appeared in exactly one prior proposal, rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_UUP_a (a static reserve-rotation spread, now DEAD in graveyard.csv), and never as a trend leg -- and the three prior single_asset_trend proposals are GLD_126, SLV_63 and VNQ_126, all commodity or real estate. Under-used primitive and untouched asset class, motivated by a policy configuration that is live right now.

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_VNQ_DBC_189_63
rationale: Structural configuration, not a track-record claim -- I assert nothing about how VNQ, DBC, real assets or any trend strategy has recently performed, and both legs are two-sided sign rules, so nothing here is a directional bet. THE MECHANISM I EXPECT TO MAKE THE TWO LEGS OFFSET, which is what this primitive requires me to name specifically. A nominal Treasury yield decomposes into a real yield and an inflation breakeven. VNQ and DBC are both real assets, but each is levered to a DIFFERENT term of that decomposition, and with opposite sign. Listed REITs are long-duration claims on lease-based cash flows, so their discount rate is the REAL yield: a rise in real yields re-rates them down more or less mechanically, independent of what inflation is doing. Broad commodities are the physical goods whose spot prices ARE a large part of the headline inflation the BREAKEVEN prices; DBC is an energy-heavy basket (WTI, Brent, heating oil, RBOB, natural gas, alongside metals and grains), so it trends with the inflation impulse itself. That gives two distinct, opposite-signed transmission channels rather than one inverse relationship: (a) a SUPPLY-driven inflation shock raises commodity prices directly (DBC leg trends up) while passing into headline inflation, raising nominal and then real policy-rate expectations, which is a headwind to the rate-sensitive real estate leg (VNQ trends down); (b) a DEMAND/growth slowdown does the reverse -- commodity demand and prices fall (DBC down) while real yields fall and REITs' stable, lease-based, largely domestic cash flows re-rate up (VNQ up). Because the two channels are different economic shocks rather than a single common factor with a sign flip, this is not a mechanical inverse pair, and its offsetting behaviour is conditional on which shock dominates. That distinction is the whole point: a mechanically anti-correlated pair would be one position wearing two tickers, whereas two channels that dominate in different regimes is what a hedge is supposed to look like -- and it is also why I expect this to clear the calibration-window decorrelation cap rather than fail it as a disguised single bet, since 2007-2017 contained both shock types (the 2008 demand collapse, the 2010-11 commodity boom, the 2014-15 oil-supply bust, and the whole disinflationary REIT re-rating) rather than one regime repeated. WHY THIS CONFIGURATION IS LIVE RIGHT NOW, which is what makes the two channels currently distinguishable rather than an abstraction. The market is presently pricing exactly channel (a), and pricing it as a term-structure phenomenon rather than a level one: the 10-year breakeven sits around 2.24-2.28% (July 2026), squarely inside the 2.0-2.6% band it has held since 2024, while the 5-year breakeven is roughly 18bp ABOVE the 10-year -- an inverted breakeven curve. That inversion is the precise signature of a near-term supply shock priced in with long-run anchoring intact, which is the state in which the two legs should diverge most. The supply shock is identified and dated: conflict-driven disruption of the Strait of Hormuz cut global supply sharply, lifting Brent about 65% (~$46/bbl) by end-March 2026 -- the largest monthly rise on record -- with further tanker attacks and strikes in early July 2026, and the EIA revising its 2026 Brent average from $58 to $79 in a single month. Meanwhile the 10-year TIPS real yield is around 2.3%, historically high, so the REIT leg's discount rate is under pressure at the same moment the commodity leg's driver is spiking. Sell-side framing of the same configuration is explicit that supply-driven inflation skews the risk toward DELAYED Fed easing, 'limiting support for rate-sensitive, cyclical sectors such as Financials and Real Estate', while noting REITs are relatively well positioned in lower-growth, higher-uncertainty states -- i.e. the same two channels, named by someone else. I am NOT proposing to trade that view: the candidate takes whatever sign each leg's own trailing return gives it. The current configuration matters only as evidence that the two channels are economically real and currently separable, which is the claim this primitive asks me to make and have checked. WEAKNESSES, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN APPENDED. (1) The dominant prior is against this: trend is the deadest family in this lab -- tsmom_*, tsmom_gen_*, donchian_*, green_line_200d are all DEAD against these same gates -- and combining two trend legs does not create edge that neither leg has. If both legs are individually unpredictable, pairing them produces a lower-variance nothing, which gate 1's DSR/CPCV test should and will reject. (2) The hedge argument is about RISK, not return; doctrine gate 2 asks whether a candidate earns its place, and a candidate whose only virtue is decorrelation is exactly the case the unapproved v1.1 diversifier clause would have been needed to rescue -- it is not approved, so this must clear the bar on its own. (3) DBC is a futures-basket ETF: its return embeds roll yield, so a leg that is long commodities much of the time collects or pays contango/backwardation independent of trend, and neither this primitive nor the gates separate the two. (4) VNQ's rate sensitivity is a well-known factor exposure, so the REIT leg may be a levered duration bet in disguise rather than a real-estate one. (5) The 2018-present OOS window contains the March 2020 shock, where both legs collapsed together and the claimed offset would have failed exactly when it mattered -- the single most likely way this dies for the right reason. PARAMETERS, DERIVED NOT SEARCHED. lookback_a=189 trading days (~9 months) for VNQ: cap-rate and discount-rate re-rating in listed real estate works through three quarterly reporting cycles and lags the rate move that causes it, so a window shorter than that reads noise and one at the 252 cap averages the re-rating away. lookback_b=63 (one quarter) for DBC: energy supply shocks pass into prices and into headline inflation within weeks, so the commodity leg's driver operates on a much faster clock than the real estate leg's -- the mismatch is the mechanism, not a fitted choice. freq=W is set by the FASTER leg: a 63-day sign can flip on any session, and a monthly clock would act up to ~21 trading days late on it (a third of that leg's own horizon), while weekly holds the lag under ~8%. Turnover cost is bounded regardless of cadence because a sign that does not flip generates no trade. DISTINCTNESS. No graveyard.csv row pairs real estate against commodities: the DEAD tsmom_*/ tsmom_gen_* families trend all 15 UNIVERSE tickers as a single ensemble in which VNQ and DBC are 1/15 each and net against thirteen others, so this two-leg structure has never been isolated. In this ledger the three prior asset_class_trend_hedge proposals are SPY/GLD, TLT/DBC and SPY/IEF -- every one of them anchors on an equity or rates leg, and none touches real_estate, which is the asset class with the fewest appearances here. The one prior VNQ proposal, rp_single_asset_trend_VNQ_126, is a different primitive at a different lookback, and rp_static_spread_carry_VNQ_IEF_a is a static always-on spread with no trend component; neither leg of this candidate duplicates an existing spec. Chosen partly for that breadth -- asset_class_trend_hedge is under-used (3 of 21 prior proposals against static_spread_carry's 6) -- but the mechanism above is the reason, not the tally.

name: rp_curve_carry_63
rationale: The 2s10s slope's two drivers have split onto different clocks in 2026, which is what makes a slope-momentum signal structurally interesting right now rather than a generic trend bet. The front end is being pulled down by a Fed easing toward a 3.0-3.5% funds rate over the course of 2026, a slow and largely pre-announced path; the long end is being held up by fiscal supply and term-premium normalization, which arrives in discrete bursts on the quarterly refunding calendar (the August 2026 refunding is $125bn of 3s/10s/30s including $25bn of 30-year, raising ~$28.7bn of new cash). The result on 2026-08-04 is 2y 4.21% / 10y 4.63% / 30y 5.20% -- a 2s10s of only ~42bp, far below the 100-150bp of a normal expansion, with the ACM 10-year term premium at 0.79% on 2026-07-30, clearly positive for the first time since 2023. A slope repriced by supply absorption moves in refunding-cycle-length steps, not smooth macro drift, so the pre-registered horizon here is 63 trading days -- one full quarterly refunding cycle -- measuring the change in slope across a complete supply cycle rather than intra-cycle auction noise. Monthly rebalance because a signal that only refreshes on a quarterly cadence has nothing to say at finer resolution, and the DV01-neutral TLT/IEF construction earns a small duration-differential that faster turnover would swamp. Distinct from rp_curve_carry_126 (W, proposed earlier on 2026-08-06), which spans two refunding cycles at weekly resolution and therefore averages across exactly the cycle boundary this spec is built to sit on. Honest prior: this lab has killed every predictive strategy it has tested, and curve_carry is trend-following applied to a slope rather than a price -- the reason to test it is that its input is a real macro-structural series with a named, currently-operating supply mechanism, not that trend-following deserves another look.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_EEM_EFA_a
rationale: Structural, not a track-record claim -- and the strongest current fact I found cuts AGAINST the trade, which is why it is stated in the middle rather than buried. This is the first use of EEM anywhere in this pipeline ledger and the first attempt in this lab at the emerging-market equity risk premium: graveyard.csv contains no EEM row at all, and the only prior roster appearance of the pair is family N's pre-registered EFA/EEM cointegration test, which FAILED the ADF stationarity filter on 2007-2017 (beta 0.826, ADF p=0.551) and therefore never traded OOS. THE PREMIUM. A fixed, always-on long EEM / short EFA is the canonical harvest direction of the segmentation/country-risk premium: emerging equity markets are only partially integrated with world capital markets, so their cost of equity carries a country-risk component -- political, expropriation, capital-control, institutional and local-liquidity risk -- that developed markets' does not, and country-risk measures predict future equity returns in emerging markets and NOT in developed ones, which is the empirical signature of that segmentation. The spread is paid for bearing that risk, with no directional forecast of either leg -- the same shape as this lab's one surviving carry book (crypto funding), where the return is compensation for a real tail risk rather than a prediction. WHY EFA IS THE SHORT LEG AND NOT SPY. Both legs are USD-unhedged foreign equity, so the common dollar-versus-foreign-currency beta partially cancels and what is left is closer to a clean EM-versus-developed-ex-US claim rather than a disguised short-dollar bet; and it avoids shorting the record US mega-cap AI concentration that an earlier proposal in this same ledger (rp_static_spread_carry_IWM_SPY_a) identified as contaminating any SPY short leg. THE STRUCTURAL BACKDROP, stated as backdrop and explicitly NOT as the premium: the IMF's 2026 WEO puts advanced-economy growth at 1.8% for 2026 against 3.8% for emerging market and developing economies (recovering to 4.5% in 2027), and EM entered this cycle with more monetary easing room after the 2021-22 tightening and lower public-debt ratios than DM, where policy rates are constrained by debt dynamics. Faster growth is a forecast, not a risk premium, and no part of this candidate's claim rests on it; it matters only because a segmentation premium is harder to argue is compensation for distress when the distress is not visibly increasing. THE FACT THAT CUTS AGAINST IT, and the single strongest reason this candidate may deserve to die: MSCI EM is no longer a diversified emerging-risk basket. As of 2026-06-18 the index is Taiwan 27.01%, Korea 24.87%, China 18.67%, India 10.68% -- Taiwan and Korea alone are over 51%, IT is close to 37% of the index, and Taiwan semiconductors are 16.2% on their own; Korea passed China for the first time during 2026 on a semiconductor-driven index reweighting. So long EEM / short EFA is in substance TWO bets: long a country-risk premium, and long a concentrated semiconductor and AI-hardware block against a diversified developed-ex-US index. Only the first is a risk premium; the second is an idiosyncratic sector bet this construction never intended to take, and it is the exact mirror of the concentration problem already identified on SPY's side in this ledger. The hypothesis actually under test is therefore narrower and more honest than 'does EM pay a premium': does a segmentation premium survive being levered onto a two-country semiconductor concentration? The wide EM valuation discount (MSCI EM forward P/E around 11.6 at 2026-01-01, quoted near 14x on 2026 estimates elsewhere) is cited as a SYMPTOM of that composition and of the segmentation discount itself, never as a cheapness signal -- there is no valuation timing in this construction. KNOWN NEGATIVE RUNNING COST, up front. EEM's expense ratio is roughly 0.7% against roughly 0.32% for EFA, so about 38bp/yr of any premium is paid away in fund fees before a single unit of risk is compensated, and EM dividend withholding is heavier than DM's on top of that. Unlike a mechanically-paid funding rate, this premium has to clear a known fee drag first. THE HONEST PRIOR. EM underperformed developed markets for most of the 2010s, so the modern-era record of this exact spread is against it, and I am not appealing to any more recent stretch to argue otherwise -- doing so would be the selection-on-results this ledger exists to avoid. The OOS window (2018-present) contains at least three episodes that should punish this construction hard if the premium is not real: the 2018 dollar and trade-war drawdown, March 2020, and the 2021-22 China regulatory crackdown and property bust, all cases where EM fell further than DM. If the average premium does not survive those net of the fee drag above, gate 1's DSR against a duty-cycle-matched null or gate 3's pain test should kill it; that is the hypothesis under test, not a caveat appended to a bullish case. ON PRIMITIVE CHOICE, since static_spread_carry is the most-used primitive in this ledger (6 of 23 rows) and breadth is preferred: the two under-used primitives were both worse choices TODAY, not by default. curve_carry (2 uses) has a one-dimensional parameter space and already received two proposals within the last four hours (lookback 126 and 63) -- a third lookback today would be an LLM-run parameter sweep of a single mechanism, exactly the multiple-testing shape DOCTRINE.md warns about. cross_sectional_rank (3 uses) has had each of its three metrics proposed within the last 30 hours, and its low_vol arm is the most exhaustively factory-swept mechanism in graveyard.csv (roughly 30 low_vol_xsec_gen_* verdicts spanning 16d to 179d lookbacks, every one DEAD with negative OOS Sharpe). The research I actually did supports a structural carry claim, and static_spread_carry is its only home in the current vocabulary. freq M matches a static spread whose only turnover is the rebalance back to fixed weights.

name: rp_curve_carry_252
rationale: The 2s10s slope's current re-steepening is driven by two structurally distinct, slow-moving forces that push the same way and both run on a multi-quarter clock, not a meeting-to-meeting one. (a) The front end is being pulled down by a measured, multi-year easing cycle -- 175bp of cuts since Sep 2024 to a 3.50-3.75% target, with consensus for roughly 3.00-3.25% by end-2026 -- so DGS2 steps down slowly and predictably. (b) The long end is held up by a positive and rising term premium sourced from fiscal supply: $2T+ annual deficits plus balance-sheet runoff force private absorption of a growing share of long-dated paper against foreign official demand that has plateaued since 2014, so DGS10 does not follow the front end down. The result is a normalization that is explicitly mid-course rather than finished: 2s10s un-inverted in Sep 2024, only achieved a sustained positive slope across tenors in Q4 2025, and sat at roughly 42bp on 2026-08-04 (DGS2 4.21%, DGS10 4.63%) -- still well below the 100-150bp range typical of a normal expansion. curve_carry trend-follows this slope with a DV01-neutral TLT/IEF position, so the only real choice here is which timescale of slope change the signal measures. Both prior pipeline curve_carry proposals sample the short end of the pre-registered range (63d, 126d), which resolves the FOMC/CPI/auction repricing sitting ON TOP of the normalization rather than the normalization itself; 252d -- the top of the range -- measures slope change over a full year, matching the clock of the two drivers above. Monthly rebalance is the honest turnover match for a signal whose sign at a 252d lookback changes on a quarters-to-years cadence. Proposed as a structural hypothesis about a mechanism and its timescale, not from any claim about slope trades' recent results -- a year-scale slope trend this widely narrated may well already be priced, which is what the OOS gate is for.

The ticker's dominant fundamental driver has therefore CHANGED -- from broad EM growth/commodity/currency beta to the capacity cycle of the AI semiconductor supply chain -- and that is a composition fact checkable from holdings data, not a view. MECHANISM. A trailing-sign rule monetizes something only when the asset's dominant driver is serially correlated. Contracted manufacturing capacity is serially correlated by industrial construction rather than by sentiment: DRAM capacity is reported effectively sold out through 2026 and into 2027, and TSMC lifted its 2026 capex plan to $60-64bn from $52-56bn. Underneath sits the textbook slow-adjusting capital stock -- a leading-edge fab takes roughly 2-3 years to build -- so the industry's capacity/price cycle over- and under-shoots on a multi-year clock. That persistence is symmetric: an over-capacity downswing is as slow as an upswing, which is why this is a persistence claim and not a bullish one. The concentration that gives the driver its persistence also makes this a single-supply-chain bet wearing an EM label: a Taiwan/Korea geopolitical event, an export-control change, or one company's process failure would dominate the signal, and none of those are serially correlated at all -- the diversification the 'EM' label implies is largely gone, and that concentration is itself being flagged as an index-level risk. name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_GLD_126_189
rationale: STRUCTURAL COMPOSITION, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM. I assert nothing about how trend signals, gold, long Treasuries, or any live strategy has recently performed; a trailing-sign rule takes BOTH directions on each leg, so nothing here forecasts a direction for either. THE SPECIFIC MECHANISM MAKING THESE TWO LEGS OFFSET (v1.14 requires a named one, not an uncorrelatedness claim): official-sector reserve substitution. Long-dated Treasuries and gold are the two dominant instruments in the same balance sheet -- global official FX reserves -- and a reallocation between them mechanically removes demand from one leg and adds it to the other. That reallocation is documented and large: gold overtook US Treasuries as the world's second-largest official reserve asset by end-2025 (gold's share of official reserves 20% in 2024 -> 27% in 2025, Treasuries down to 22%), central banks bought a net 244 tonnes in Q1 2026 alone, and 74% of reserve managers surveyed expect moderate-to-significantly lower USD reserve holdings over the next five years. The Treasury side of that same shift is visible as a price: the NY Fed ACM 10y term premium is positive for the first time since 2023 and topped 50bp for the first time since 2014, with the long end the most exposed point on the curve precisely because the price-insensitive foreign official bid was concentrated there -- 30y ~5.15-5.20% against a 10y ~4.6% that touched an 18-month high of ~4.75% this week, and $2T+ annual deficits keeping issuance at the 20y/30y points heavy. So the driver of the TLT leg right now is sovereign supply and issuer risk, not growth or inflation expectations. WHY THIS IS A REGIME-DEPENDENT RELATIONSHIP, WHICH IS THE SHAPE THIS PRIMITIVE'S CORRELATION GUARD ACTUALLY WANTS. When the long end is driven by growth scares, TLT and GLD are substitutes and rally together (positive relationship). When it is driven by fiscal supply and issuer risk -- the current regime, per the term-premium evidence above -- gold absorbs exactly the sovereign-risk hedging demand that long Treasuries shed, and the relationship inverts. A relationship that flips sign across regimes is what can carry a real economic mechanism while still clearing an unconditional |corr| <= 0.3 cap; a permanently offsetting pair could not. PARAMETERIZATION, MATCHED TO EACH DRIVER'S OWN CLOCK. lookback_a=126 (~6 months) on TLT spans two consecutive quarterly refunding cycles, so the leg's sign reflects the supply/term-premium impulse rather than one auction or one CPI print. lookback_b=189 (~9 months, three quarters) on GLD matches the cadence at which official reserve accumulation is actually decided and reported (quarterly WGC/IMF reserve data, annual allocation mandates) -- deliberately SLOWER than the rates leg, which no prior asset_class_trend_hedge draw here has done (252/252, 252/60, 252/63, 189/63 all run the second leg at or faster than the first). Monthly rebalance is the honest turnover match for two multi-quarter signals under v1.5's duty-cycle-matched null. VOCABULARY BREADTH: asset_class_trend_hedge is tied for least-used in this ledger (4 of 28 rows), TLT+GLD is an untested leg pair here, and graveyard.csv contains no TLT/GLD row of any kind. WHAT CUTS AGAINST IT, STATED BEFORE THE RESULT IS KNOWN. (1) The mechanism I cite is largely POST-2022 (sanctions, reserve fragmentation, the fiscal-supply regime), while the calibration window that screens this candidate is 2007-2017 -- an era when TLT and GLD were both QE/disinflation beneficiaries. Their calibration-window trend signs may well correlate above CALIB_CORR_CAP=0.3 and get this mechanically rejected. I am not asserting it passes; the guard exists to decide that, and a rejection here would be a correct outcome, not a defect in the proposal. (2) v1.14 names the real hazard directly: two zero-edge trend legs can look like they earn their place through variance reduction alone. Nothing in this rationale is evidence either leg has an edge. (3) Prior probability is low on this lab's own record -- 139+ strategies tested, 0 ALIVE predictive, and four sibling asset_class_trend_hedge rows already rest on related cross-class arguments.

name: rp_pair_zscore_HYG_LQD_90_2p0_4p0
rationale: US credit enters August 2026 at a historic tightness extreme: high-yield index OAS is ~281bp, inside the richest decile of its history against a long-run median near 450bp, while investment grade sits at ~81bp -- and the HY/IG ratio is near its long-run ~3.5x, i.e. the richness is market-wide rather than a quality-tier distortion. That is a structural asymmetry in the HYG-vs-LQD relative price, not a directional view: with HY already in its richest decile there is very little remaining spread-compression headroom for HYG to keep grinding richer against LQD, while the widening episodes that do occur are sharp and are pulled back by HY's much larger carry -- a bounded, snap-back distribution is exactly the shape a z-scored log-spread mean-reversion signal is built for, and the opposite of the one-way drift that kills this primitive on a trending ratio. Two current conditions reinforce it. (1) Rate volatility is dormant (MOVE ~75, having touched ~59 in late 2025), so the HYG/LQD duration mismatch (HYG ~3yr vs LQD ~8yr) injects less rates noise into the log-spread than in a high-rate-vol regime -- the spread is closer to a pure credit-quality signal now than it usually is. (2) Investment-grade gross supply is forecast at ~$2.25tn for 2026, a ~35% YoY increase that could outpace demand for the first time since 2022 -- an identified LQD-specific pressure, i.e. a source of relative dislocation for the ratio to revert from rather than a trend either leg should ride. Deliberately NOT the always-on long-HY carry bet already proposed as rp_static_spread_carry_HYG_LQD_a (2026-08-04): at the richest decile an always-on structural bet is the worst-priced version of this trade, which is precisely why the dislocate-and-revert shape is the one worth testing. z_window=90 (~4.5 months) spans a full credit-spread dislocation cycle rather than a single risk-off week; entry 2.0 / stop 4.0 keeps the standard band this primitive's earlier proposals used; weekly rebalance because credit-ETF relative dislocations resolve over weeks, and this is the first pair_zscore proposal at a frequency other than daily, where turnover cost dominates a spread trade. Structural/valuation reasoning only -- no claim about any strategy's recent performance.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_momentum_63_3
rationale: Cross-asset return dispersion is at a genuine structural extreme in 2026, and it is wide across exactly the asset classes UNIVERSE spans rather than inside any single one. Concrete instances: the gold/oil ratio sits near 55 (early-2026 readings ~75:1 with gold ~$5,000/oz against oil ~$67/bbl) versus a since-1900 average near 20 and a modern average ~22 -- the far right tail of its whole historical distribution, matched only by April 2020 and the 1980s oil crises; 2026 asset-class performance spans roughly +94.5% (silver) to -20% (natural gas); and fixed income's own 2026 theme is explicitly dispersion 'across sectors, structures, and parts of the curve' rather than a uniform beta-driven opportunity set. Cboe's DSPX implied-dispersion index independently hit a 6-year high of 47% in the week of 2026-07-13, above its April 'Liberation Day' peak -- that one measures single-stock dispersion inside SPY, not cross-asset dispersion, so it is corroborating context here, not the load-bearing fact. Why this matters mechanically for THIS primitive and not as a performance claim: a cross-sectional long-short's gross payoff is the top-K minus bottom-K return spread, which scales directly with the dispersion of the cross-section it ranks. Wide dispersion does not make the ranking correct -- it raises the payoff per unit of ranking accuracy, and equally the loss per unit of ranking error. That is the structural condition; whether momentum ranking has any accuracy at all is precisely what the doctrine's gates are being asked to decide. Why momentum as the metric, and why 63 days: the same 2026 research describes elevated structural breaks across many cross-asset pairs simultaneously (gold rising alongside real yields, the gold/oil ratio at a multi-decade extreme) -- a regime in which each asset is driven by its own idiosyncratic, slow-moving macro driver (central-bank and ETF gold demand, Treasury term premium and supply, an oil supply shock followed by ceasefire reversal) rather than by a common factor. Persistent asset-specific drivers are the structural precondition for the rank ordering itself to persist, which is all cross-sectional momentum bets on. 63 days is the short end of the standard 3-12 month formation window, chosen because the drivers above are turning over fast in a regime transition -- deliberately distinct from the two momentum draws this pipeline has already proposed (126/k=2 on 2026-08-05, 252/k=4 on 2026-08-06); this is a different formation horizon pre-registered on its own reasoning, not a re-run of either. k=3 of 15 tickers keeps both sleeves diversified within an asset class rather than concentrating the whole position in whichever single commodity is at an extreme. Monthly rebalance because a 63-day formation does not justify paying weekly or daily turnover. Honest prior: this lab has already killed cross-sectional momentum (2 graveyard rows under xsec_momentum) and 52 low_vol_xsec rows besides, and no predictive strategy here has ever survived. name: rp_static_spread_carry_SLV_GLD_a
rationale: Silver and gold share nearly all of their monetary drivers -- real rates, the dollar, ETF and central-bank demand -- so a fixed long-SLV/short-GLD spread nets those out and leaves one exposure standing: silver's industrial demand and its physical supply balance. That balance is structural, not cyclical noise. The Silver Institute / Metals Focus World Silver Survey 2026 (published 2026-04-15) puts 2026 at a SIXTH consecutive annual market deficit of 46.3 Moz, up 15% from 40.3 Moz in 2025, and the deficit is widening even though total demand is forecast to fall ~2% -- because mine and scrap supply are falling faster (~-2%). Cumulatively 762 Moz has been drawn from above-ground stocks since 2021, so the inventory buffer absorbing the gap is finite and measurably smaller each year. Industrial use ran ~680 Moz in 2024, roughly 60% of total demand, with solar PV alone at ~120-125 Moz against a 665 GW 2026 install forecast. That industrial share is precisely the risk being borne, and it is why this is a carry bet rather than a forecast: the long leg carries a real industrial and solar-capex cycle that the short leg does not, and it gets punished hard when that cycle turns -- the gold-silver ratio sat above 100 as recently as 2025 before trading in the ~55-65 range in 2026, which is the drawdown scale this spread can inflict, not a reason to expect it to keep going. The proposal rests on the deficit and the demand mix, not on the recent direction of the ratio. Monthly rebalance because the position has no timing content at all -- it is always-on, and the only turnover is drift correction. Distinct from rp_pair_zscore_GLD_SLV_60_2p0_4p0 (proposed 2026-08-05), which tests this same spread as MEAN-REVERSION around its own rolling mean; this is a bet on the spread's level, the same distinction rp_static_spread_carry_TLT_IEF_a drew against family N's cointegration row. No SLV/GLD static spread appears anywhere in graveyard.csv or pipeline_ideas.csv.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_USO_126
rationale: Crude oil's forward curve is in a documented, persistent CONTANGO right now, and USO is the one UNIVERSE instrument whose returns are dominated by front-month WTI roll mechanics rather than by spot alone -- DBC is a broad, roll-optimised multi-commodity basket in which the oil curve is diluted, and no other UNIVERSE ticker touches the curve at all. Structural setup as of August 2026: WTI and Brent are in clear contango, dropping roughly $20/bbl between the August 2026 and early-2030s maturities; the IEA's July 2026 Oil Market Report projects a 3.7-4.0 mb/d oversupply and notes global inventories rose at their fastest pace since 2020; the EIA's July 2026 STEO forecasts inventory builds averaging 2.7 mb/d in 4Q26 and 5.0 mb/d through 2027; OPEC has flipped its Q3 call from deficit to surplus. The MECHANISM being tested is not 'trend works' -- this lab has killed every trend strategy it has run, and that prior is taken seriously. It is narrower and specific to this instrument in this regime: USO rolls near-dated WTI futures monthly, so a contango curve makes that roll structurally negative -- it sells the cheaper expiring contract and buys a costlier deferred one, and NAV decays against spot regardless of direction. A trailing-return sign signal is SHORT whenever that decay has already shown up in its window, so in a surplus regime the trend leg and the roll drag point the same way instead of fighting each other; in a balanced or backwardated market they fight, which is the honest reason trend on oil has no general edge. That asymmetry is the testable claim, and the OOS gate decides it, not this rationale. lookback=126 (~6 months) matches the regime's own timescale, which the EIA/IEA forecasts put in quarters-to-years, and is deliberately long enough not to whipsaw on the geopolitical spikes that repeatedly reversed within weeks during 2026 (June's wartime gains were fully erased as Gulf tanker traffic recovered) while still short enough to turn if the surplus resolves. Monthly rebalance for the same duty-cycle reason DOCTRINE v1.5b's matched null exists: a semiannual signal should not be traded faster than it actually changes. New to this pipeline: USO has never been proposed under single_asset_trend (prior legs GLD/SLV/VNQ/UUP/EEM), and its only prior appearances are as the a-leg of static_spread_carry USO/DBC and pair_zscore USO/DBC -- both relative-value against the same basket, neither a directional test of the roll drag itself. On vocabulary breadth: curve_carry is the least-used primitive (4 proposals) but its sole parameter is lookback and 21/63/126/252 are already taken, so a fifth would be near-duplicative; single_asset_trend is tied-lowest among the rest at 5.

name: rp_pair_zscore_TLT_IEF_63_1p75_3p5
rationale: pair_zscore's mean-reversion premise needs a cointegration anchor -- a structural reason the two legs CANNOT permanently diverge -- and TLT/IEF is the only pair in UNIVERSE that actually has one: same issuer, same credit, same currency, differing only in the segment of the curve they sit on (~16yr vs ~7.5yr effective duration). Every pair_zscore proposal in this ledger so far crosses a credit boundary (HYG/LQD, LQD/IEF), a commodity boundary (GLD/SLV, USO/DBC) or a country boundary (EFA/SPY), where the spread can re-rate permanently and 'unusually wide' is not the same claim. Here the log-spread is mechanically a function of the 10s30s curve segment alone. STRUCTURAL CONDITIONS NOW, not a performance claim: I assert nothing about how any strategy has recently performed. (a) Long-end supply is currently a KNOWN, calendared flow rather than a surprise -- Treasury's 2026-08-05 refunding statement offers $125bn ($42bn 10y auctioned Aug 12, $25bn 30y Aug 13) and explicitly guides to unchanged nominal coupon sizes 'for at least the next several quarters'. That distinction is the whole trade: pre-announced, repeating supply produces the transient dealer-inventory concession-and-reversal the auction-cycle literature documents (Lou/Yan/Zhang 2013's inverted-V), whereas supply being revised UP unexpectedly would re-rate term premium permanently and this spread would trend instead of revert -- a falsifiable condition, not a one-way story. (b) The curve is flat and un-inverted (2s10s ~43bp on 2026-08-05, 2y 4.20 / 10y 4.63 / 30y ~5.20), so the spread is not being dragged by an ongoing inversion-to-normalization regime shift. z_window=63 spans roughly one full refunding-announcement-to-announcement cycle, so the rolling mean contains one concession and one reversal rather than half of each. z_entry=1.75 is deliberately below the 2.0 used elsewhere in this ledger because a same-issuer spread's own dispersion is far tighter than a cross-asset one, so a 3-sigma entry would essentially never fire; z_stop=3.5 is deliberately near the bottom of its (3.0,6.0) range to CUT rather than average into the one failure mode that matters -- a genuine term-premium repricing, which the 10y ACM term premium turning positive for the first time since 2023 makes a live risk, not a hypothetical. HONEST CAVEATS, stated before any result: (1) Fleming/Liu/Nguyen find auction price pressure has NOT increased in recent years, because non-dealer participants now absorb more supply and ease the dealers' intermediation burden -- the mechanism may be weaker today than the 33-year sample implies; (2) the auction cycle is documented intraday-to-a-few-days on individual on-the-run notes, whereas TLT/IEF are daily closes of duration-bucketed baskets, so the effect reaching this instrument is attenuated and partly averaged away; (3) this lab's prior on all predictive strategies is DEAD (139 in graveyard.csv, 0 ALIVE as of 2026-07-29) and nothing here asks for a lower bar. Primitive choice: pair_zscore is joint-second-least-proposed (5 of 34 rows); curve_carry is nominally the least-used (4) but its single pre-registered parameter is already drawn at 21/63/126/252 across the whole (20,252) range, so a fifth draw would explore less, not more. Note this is a DIFFERENT mechanism from curve_carry on the same two tickers: that primitive trend-follows the FRED DGS10-DGS2 slope with a DV01-neutral position; this one mean-reverts a 1:1 price log-spread and reads no external data. Not a duplicate of rp_static_spread_carry_TLT_IEF_a either -- that is an always-on term-premium harvest with no entry condition.

name: rp_curve_carry_189
rationale: The 2s10s spread has exited its 2022-2024 inversion but sat at only 0.45% on 2026-08-03 -- positive and well under the 100-150bp slope typical of an expansion -- while the 3m10y has flipped negative again in recent weeks. The two ends are being pushed by two different slow-moving forces rather than by one common level shock: the front end by an expected easing path (the 2y trades roughly 70bp below the policy rate, pricing about 100bp of cumulative cuts by mid-2028), the long end by a term premium rebuilding after five years near or below zero, with Treasury holding nominal coupon auction sizes steady for at least several more quarters even as borrowing needs climb and naming the size and composition of the SOMA portfolio as the swing variable it is positioned for. Both drivers update on a quarterly policy cadence -- refunding statements, SEP revisions, balance-sheet decisions -- and persist between updates, which is the condition a slope trend-follower needs: a slope that drifts rather than oscillates. A 189-day lookback spans roughly three of those quarterly cycles, long enough to average through announcement-day noise and short enough to stay inside the post-inversion regime. curve_carry is the least-used primitive in this ledger (4 of 35 proposals) and the only one reading real FRED curve data rather than ETF prices; nothing in graveyard.csv trades the rates-curve slope, so this is not a re-run of the price-trend space families A/B/D already swept. Distinct from the four curve_carry specs already proposed (21/63/126/252) only in horizon, which is the sole parameter this primitive has -- the quarterly-cadence argument is the reason for this specific value, fixed before any result is known.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_42_2
rationale: Cross-sectional reversal is a liquidity/risk-premium-provision payoff: it is paid when the extremes of a cross-section are there because of a transitory premium that reprices in both directions, and it is systematically wrong when one common factor dominates and trends. Current cross-asset structure is squarely the former. (1) The common factor is unusually weak -- the US stock/bond correlation coefficient ran 0.11 from the start of 2025 through mid-2026 against 0.66 in 2022, and average 3-month pairwise correlation inside the S&P 500 is ~13%, with single-stock implied vol at a historically wide premium to index vol. (2) What is generating dispersion instead is asset-class-specific shocks that round-trip on a days-to-weeks clock rather than trending: crude surged more than 20% in July 2026 on US-Iran escalation, Red Sea attacks and Strait of Hormuz risk, then fell 4% to $77.11 on a single headline about possible US-Iran talks; gold sits historically elevated near $4,100 on a safe-haven bid; the long end is repricing separately on term premium and supply, with the 30-year at 5.275%. A geopolitical risk premium that is installed and removed by headlines is the textbook transitory dislocation, and it is landing on different asset classes at different times rather than on all of them at once. Parameters follow that mechanism rather than a search: lookback 42 (~2 months) spans a full install-and-fade cycle of the July surge instead of a single leg of it; k=2 concentrates the book on the four genuinely dislocated names out of 15, since the transitory premium lives only at the extremes, not across the middle of the ranking; weekly rebalance because monthly would miss round trips that complete inside a month. Chosen partly to exercise cross_sectional_rank, the joint-least-proposed primitive in this ledger (5 of 36 prior proposals) and with only one prior reversal draw (rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_21_3, a different window and a wider book). Honest counterweights, stated up front rather than after a verdict: reversal-shaped strategies are already heavily represented in graveyard.csv as DEAD (the str_reversal_* family and its factory variants), so this deserves no benefit of the doubt and gets none -- the same DSR/CPCV gates apply; and crude's futures curve was in backwardation in late July 2026, which is a persistence argument that cuts against reversal on that specific leg.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_LQD_IEF_a
rationale: Structural, not a track-record claim -- I assert nothing about how LQD, IEF, corporate credit or any live strategy has recently performed, and no timing view is expressed: static_spread_carry holds a FIXED, always-on position, so the hypothesis under test is only whether a persistent risk premium exists, never whether now is a good entry. THE LAST MAJOR RISK PREMIUM IN THIS UNIVERSE NOT YET EXPRESSED BY THIS PRIMITIVE. The eight prior static_spread_carry proposals in this ledger cover the term premium (TLT/IEF), the credit QUALITY-TIER differential (HYG/LQD), the property/cap-rate premium (VNQ/IEF), size (IWM/SPY), EM (EEM/EFA), the commodity front-of-curve roll (USO/DBC), the industrial-vs-monetary metals split (SLV/GLD) and the official-sector reserve rotation (GLD/UUP). None of them is the investment-grade credit premium itself. HYG/LQD is a bet on the tier relationship, and current data says that relationship is the unremarkable part: the HY/IG OAS ratio is near its long-run ~3.5x, i.e. the richness in credit is MARKET-WIDE rather than a tier distortion. Long LQD / short IEF is the only pair this UNIVERSE can form that isolates the market-wide IG premium -- compensation for default, downgrade and illiquidity risk on investment-grade corporate paper, measured against Treasuries of the same maturity bucket. WHY THE PAIR IS DURATION-CLEAN, the load-bearing mechanical point. An IG credit spread is only a credit premium if the rate exposure cancels; otherwise it is a levered duration bet wearing a credit label. LQD's effective duration is 7.97yr against IEF's 7.2yr -- a residual under one year on a base of ~8 -- and engine.py's own sizing closes most of what remains, because it vol-targets EACH leg to TARGET_VOL=10% annualized on a 60-day trailing window rather than holding fixed notionals. Both legs' volatility is dominated by the same Treasury curve, so equal-vol sizing scales them to approximately equal DV01 automatically and the residual is close to a pure spread. No other pair here has that property: family N's pre-registered LQD/HYG carries credit on BOTH legs, and VNQ/IEF deliberately does not hedge duration at all. THE CURRENT STRUCTURAL CONDITION, stated as what makes the test informative rather than as a reason to expect a pass. The ICE BofA US Corporate OAS sits near 80bp -- roughly its tightest in 25 years, against a long-run average near 150bp -- with BBB near 100bp and AA near 50bp, while the broad IG index yield-to-worst has spent 2026 in a 5.0-5.4% range. The premium this candidate harvests is therefore priced at roughly HALF its own historical average. THE SINGLE BIGGEST WEAKNESS, FIRST RATHER THAN BURIED: that thinness is a reason to expect this to FAIL, and it is the honest prior going in. I propose it anyway because waiting for a wider spread would be timing, and this primitive cannot time -- a fixed always-on spread either earns an unconditional premium across the whole OOS window or it does not, and that is precisely the question worth one pre-registered test. Second weakness: the credit premium's payoff is negatively skewed and short-volatility -- long stretches of small spread accrual punctuated by sharp drawdowns -- the same shape as this lab's one surviving carry book, but WEAKER in kind, because crypto funding is a mechanically paid rate while IG spread income arrives net of realized defaults and downgrades that are small, lumpy and correlated with exactly the episodes that hurt the position. WHAT THE OOS WINDOW WILL ACTUALLY DECIDE. 2018-present contains the realizations that should punish this construction if the premium is not real: March 2020, when IG OAS blew out from roughly 100bp to ~370bp and LQD additionally traded at a discount to NAV until the Fed's corporate-credit facilities were announced -- the worst single realization available -- and 2022, when spreads widened while rates rose, so the partial duration residual and the credit leg lost together. If the average premium does not survive those drawdowns net of costs, this should and will die on gate 3 or on gate 2's Calmar test. PRIMITIVE-CHOICE HONESTY: static_spread_carry is the MOST-proposed primitive in this ledger (8 of 37 prior proposals), so this is deliberately not a breadth pick. The justification is that the mechanism is a fixed spread, not a trend, a cross-sectional rank or a curve slope, so no under-used primitive can express it; curve_carry, the least-used, is fixed to TLT/IEF and reads no credit data at all. DISTINCT FROM WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: no graveyard.csv row uses LQD/IEF, and family N's six pre-registered cointegration pairs (GLD/SLV, TLT/IEF, EFA/EEM, SPY/QQQ, USO/DBC, LQD/HYG) do not include it. rp_pair_zscore_LQD_IEF_120_2p0_4p0 touches the same two tickers but tests a different hypothesis about the series -- reversion around a stable mean versus a persistent premium in its drift -- under a different primitive, a different name and its own separate verdict, so neither borrows the other's evidence. freq=M because the position is fixed: the only turnover is the monthly rebalance back to vol-target weights, and monthly is the lowest-turnover clock this primitive offers, which matters directly because gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched and pays the same trading costs the candidate does.

name: rp_single_asset_trend_TLT_126
rationale: Structural configuration of the long end, not a track-record claim -- I assert nothing about how TLT, duration, or any trend strategy has recently performed, and a sign rule takes BOTH directions, so nothing here is a directional call on rates. The pre-registered condition a single-ticker trailing-sign rule needs is that a KNOWN repricing arrives in installments rather than in one jump (Hong & Stein's gradual-information-diffusion condition), and the long end is currently the one place in this UNIVERSE where the price driver is explicitly a slow-moving quantity rather than an expectations jump. Two facts define that setup as of this proposal. (1) Long-maturity yields are being set by TERM PREMIUM -- fiscal deficits, net coupon issuance, SOMA runoff, foreign demand -- rather than by the expected policy path: the ACM term-premium estimate has swung ~118bp between 2020 and 2026, and with the funds rate being eased the 2y is anchored while the 10y/30y is free to drift on supply and absorption. Supply-absorption pressure is a stock that accumulates quarter by quarter as the private sector takes down a rising share of long-dated paper; it does not arrive as a single dated surprise the way a CPI print or an FOMC decision does. (2) The August 2026 quarterly refunding makes the installment cadence explicit and calendar-bound: Treasury is HOLDING nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes steady for at least the next several quarters while borrowing needs climb, financing the gap at the bill end and stating that current sizes leave it 'positioned to respond to possible changes in the fiscal outlook and in the size and composition of the SOMA portfolio.' Any future shift of marginal financing toward the long end is therefore a discrete, pre-announced, quarterly-cadence decision whose duration-supply consequences are absorbed over the following quarters -- a staircase, not a step. A 126-trading-day (~6-month, two refunding cycles) lookback with monthly rebalancing is chosen to match that cadence rather than to chase price noise. A secondary structural point for why the SIGN-CONDITIONED shape is the right one here rather than a static duration position: the stock-bond correlation is expected to sit in positive territory in this inflation regime, so duration is not currently a dependable portfolio hedge and a rule that will hold duration short as readily as long is the honest way to express it. Falsifiable in the usual way -- if long-end pricing is dominated by unforecastable auction-day and inflation-print surprises rather than by slow supply absorption, a trailing-sign rule on TLT captures nothing and this dies on gate 1 like every other trend candidate in this lab. Also fills a real gap in the pipeline's own coverage: single_asset_trend has been proposed six times, on commodity, real-estate, currency and EM-equity tickers, and never once on a rates ticker.

Term-premium regime: Ferrante Capital, 'Term Premium Is Back: Why the 10-Year Hasn't Rallied' (ferrantecapitaladvisers.com/insights/treasury-term-premium-regime-2026/) and Convex, '30Y Treasury Yield Forecast 2026' (convextrade.com/forecast/dgs30) -- ACM term-premium swing of ~118bp 2020-2026, $2T+ annual deficits plus Fed balance-sheet runoff shifting long-dated absorption to the private sector. Stock-bond correlation regime: Oxford Economics, 'Stock bond correlation will become positive again in 2026' (oxfordeconomics.com/resource/stock-bond-correlation-will-become-positive-again-in-2026/). Mechanism: Hong & Stein (1999), 'A Unified Theory of Underreaction, Momentum Trading and Overreaction in Asset Markets', Journal of Finance 54(6).

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_VNQ_UUP_126_63
rationale: A rate-sensitivity offset claim about two legs on two different clocks, not a performance claim: I assert nothing about how REITs, the dollar, or any trend strategy has recently done, and both legs are bidirectional trailing-sign rules, so nothing here is a directional call on rates, VNQ or the dollar. The specific mechanism I expect to make the legs offset is that a single identifiable driver -- the US policy-rate path -- currently reaches these two tickers with OPPOSITE sign, through two structurally distinct channels. Channel A (VNQ, real_estate): listed REITs run debt/EBITDA of roughly 5-10x against under 3x for investment-grade industrials, so their equity is a levered claim on refinancing cost, and 2026 is the year that cost is actually being crystallised -- about $875bn of commercial and multifamily mortgage debt matures in 2026 (~17% of the ~$5tn outstanding, with another ~$652bn in 2027), and loans written 5 years ago at 3-4% are rolling into 6-7% money. Nareit's Q1 2026 implied cap rates (industrial 5.2%, self-storage 5.9%, retail 6.2%, residential 6.4%, office 7.7%) sit well above the 3.0-3.5% cap rates much 2019-21 paper was underwritten at, which is what makes the refi channel bind rather than being absorbed. A hawkish repricing therefore pushes VNQ's trailing return DOWN via coverage and cap rates. Channel B (UUP, currency): the dollar's dominant driver right now is explicitly the Fed path under Chair Warsh and the US-vs-G10 policy gap, with DXY near 99.9 at the start of August 2026, 10y around 4.68%, and officials signalling readiness to hike 25bp in September if the coming inflation prints run hot. The same hawkish repricing widens the differential and pushes UUP's trailing return UP. Opposite-signed responses to one shared driver is the checkable relationship the primitive asks for -- not an observation that the two happen to be uncorrelated. The two lookbacks are deliberately unequal because the two channels run on different clocks, which is the reason this primitive gives each leg its own: 126d for VNQ because the maturity wall arrives as quarterly cohorts across 2026-27, an installment repricing whose price impact accumulates over roughly two quarters rather than in one jump; 63d for UUP because the differential channel resolves on the FOMC-plus-CPI cadence, and ~1 quarter spans about two meetings and the inflation prints the September question hinges on. Monthly rebalancing matches both drivers -- neither a quarterly refi cohort nor a meeting cycle emits new information at daily frequency, so a finer freq would buy turnover, not signal. Under-used-primitive note: asset_class_trend_hedge has 6 prior proposals and this real_estate-vs-currency pairing is unused; it is distinguishable from the TLT/UUP proposal of 2026-08-07, which put the pure duration channel on both sides, whereas leg A here is a levered cap-rate/coverage claim rather than a duration one. Stated honestly as a hypothesis: the offset claim is exactly what the calibration-window (2007-2017) correlation cap is there to test, and a 2007-2017 sample containing both the 2008 dollar spike against collapsing REITs and the 2014-15 period when a strong dollar coincided with rising REITs may well reject it. If the guard rejects it, the guard is right and this proposal should die there.

name: rp_curve_carry_84
rationale: The US curve is in a term-premium-driven BEAR steepener, not a growth/easing-cycle steepener. The FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 for the fifth straight meeting with three members dissenting FOR a hike, while the 30y reached ~5.27% (highest since 2007) against a 2y near 4.29% -- the long end repricing faster than the front end on heavy deficit-funding issuance, sticky inflation and investors demanding more term premium. That distinction is the whole mechanism here. A policy-driven slope move is anchored to a Fed reaction function and mean-reverts as the cycle turns; a supply/term-premium-driven one is a slow, structural repricing of the duration risk premium that accumulates over months, which is the persistence a slope trend-follower needs and the regime in which the DGS10-DGS2 slope should trend rather than oscillate. curve_carry is also the right SHAPE for this specific setup rather than an outright duration bet: the level is genuinely two-sided right now (prediction markets price zero cuts for all of 2026 alongside live September hike risk), so a DV01-neutral TLT/IEF position that cancels level exposure isolates the one variable whose driver is currently one-directional and fiscal. lookback=84 (~4 trailing months) matches the horizon over which this episode has actually been building -- described as the sharpest steepening since April -- long enough to ignore single-auction and single-CPI whipsaw, short enough not to average the current repricing against the flatter regime that preceded it. freq=W because issuance calendars and inflation prints move term premium on a weekly-to-monthly clock, so daily rebalancing would pay turnover for signal that has not refreshed. Chosen partly because curve_carry is this pipeline's least-proposed primitive (5 of 40 prior rows) and no prior proposal has used an ~84-day slope lookback. Prior beliefs unchanged: every predictive strategy in this lab is DEAD so far, and a plausible macro story is not evidence -- this is a hypothesis for the pre-registered OOS gate to kill, not a forecast.

name: rp_pair_zscore_HYG_SPY_63_2p0_3p5
rationale: Structural, not performance-motivated. US high-yield option-adjusted spread sits at roughly 271bp (2026-08-06) and IG OAS near 74bp in Q3 2026 -- both close to their tightest levels in about 25 years, against a long-run IG average near 150bp. A cushion that thin changes the SHAPE of the HY claim, not just its level: under the Merton structural view corporate debt is short a put on firm value, and as the spread compresses that put moves far out of the money, so the debt claim's payoff becomes closer to linear in firm value and its co-movement with the issuer's equity tightens mechanically. HYG and SPY are therefore currently two claims on the same corporate cash flows driven by one dominant common factor (corporate risk appetite), which is exactly the precondition a 1:1 log-spread z-score needs -- a stable anchor, so deviations read as transient flow/liquidity dislocations rather than a drifting fundamental. z_window=63 (one quarter of trading days) spans the ETF-flow and index-rebalance cycles that generate those dislocations. The tighter-than-usual stop (3.5 rather than the 4.0 used on most prior pair proposals here) follows from the same structural fact rather than from tuning: with the cushion this thin, a move beyond 3.5 sigma is more likely a genuine credit repricing (the put coming back into the money) than a dislocation, so the position should be flat rather than pressing. Distinct from this pipeline's earlier credit pairs, which paired credit against credit or against Treasuries (rp_pair_zscore_HYG_LQD_90_2p0_4p0, rp_pair_zscore_LQD_IEF_120_2p0_4p0, rp_static_spread_carry_HYG_LQD_a) -- this one crosses the capital structure instead. Honest caveat on the evidence: direct HTTP egress to FRED was blocked this run, so the spread levels come from web-search summaries, not a primary pull; two independently-phrased sources agree on ~270-275bp HY, which is why it is used, and nothing else in this rationale depends on an unverified number.

IG OAS ~74bp, 'fully valued', Q3 2026: https://www.breckinridge.com/insights/q3-2026-corporate-bond-market-outlook ; IG near 80bp described as tightest in ~25 years vs ~150bp long-term average: https://investmentgrade.com/investment-grade-bond-statistics-2026/ . name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_low_vol_252_2
rationale: The long end is repricing term premium -- the 30y has broken out to ~5.275% while the Fed is expected to keep easing the front end, and the stock-bond correlation has turned positive -- so the realized volatility in this ETF universe now sits in long-duration rates, the leg a cross-asset book conventionally treats as its quiet one. A cross-sectional low_vol rank makes no assumption about which asset class is defensive: it ranks each ETF by its own trailing realized vol, so it structurally shorts whatever is actually carrying the risk right now (long duration, and precious metals in a central-bank-demand-driven bull cycle) and holds the genuinely quiet legs. lookback=252 so the rank reflects the year-long term-premium repricing rather than one month of headlines; k=2 keeps both sleeves at the true extremes; freq=M matches how slowly a 252-day vol rank can move, so turnover cost is not paid for noise.

name: rp_curve_carry_42
rationale: Structural, not performance-motivated. The 2s10s slope has made a full round trip inside 2026 -- roughly 51bp in late March, a low near 27bp in late June, back to ~43bp on 2026-08-05 (10y 4.63%, 2y 4.20%) -- and is still far below the 100-150bp typical of an expansion, after the record ~27-month inversion of Jul-2022 to late-2024. What is driving that round trip is monetary-policy repricing rather than a growth shock: the FOMC held at 3.50-3.75% on 2026-07-29 on a divided 9-3 vote with three dissents FOR a hike, the June dot plot penciled one 25bp hike by year-end, and the market has been pricing a possible September hike off oil-linked inflation from the Iran conflict. That is the mechanism this primitive needs: when the modal policy path is the contested variable, each datapoint shifts the front end against the long end and the shift persists for weeks while the path is re-priced, so slope CHANGES trend over a multi-week horizon instead of mean-reverting bar to bar. lookback=42 is set to the observed timescale of that repricing -- the Mar-to-Jun flattening and the Jun-to-Aug re-steepening each ran roughly six to ten weeks, i.e. about two trading months. Prior pipeline curve_carry candidates sit at 21/63/84/126/189/252 and none measures that window: 189-252d still reads the 2025 easing regime, 21d reads a single CPI print. freq=W because the sign of a 42-day slope change can only flip on a multi-week horizon, so weekly rebalancing acts on it while daily would pay vol-retargeting turnover for movement the signal cannot contain. The DV01-neutral TLT/IEF construction is the part that matters most under current conditions specifically: the LEVEL of the 10y is being set by energy and inflation shocks (CPI 4.2% y/y in May 2026 on +15.7% energy, then 3.5% in June once the ceasefire unwound the spike), and stock-bond correlation has been positive since 2022, so an outright duration position right now is a leveraged bet on the oil-inflation path that also co-moves with equity risk. Offsetting the two legs' duration strips that level exposure out and leaves the slope -- the component the Fed reaction function actually sets. Prior: this lab has killed every predictive strategy it has tested, so the honest expectation is DEAD; the claim here is only that the current policy regime is a defensible reason to test the two-month point of a pre-registered primitive's range, and the calibration-window hedge-effectiveness guard will reject the duration-neutrality claim mechanically if it does not hold in 2007-2017 data.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_SLV_USO_a
rationale: The two commodity sub-complexes inside UNIVERSE are, right now, under opposite physical-supply regimes, which is the structural condition a fixed always-on long-short is built to harvest. Silver is in its sixth consecutive year of structural deficit -- roughly 65-70 Moz short in 2026 on a cumulative 2021-2026 shortfall of ~1,050-1,100 Moz (more than a full year of mine production) drawn down from above-ground stocks, with industrial use ~60% of total demand and solar PV alone absorbing ~120-125 Moz against ~665 GW of 2026 installs; mine supply is rigid because ~70% of silver is a by-product of copper/lead/zinc/gold output and does not respond to the silver price. Crude is in the mirror-image position: OPEC+ added 188 kbpd in August 2026 as it unwinds cuts, Persian Gulf supply recovers to ~90% of pre-war volumes in August and near-full by November, the IEA puts the 2026 surplus at nearly 4 mb/d with the first monthly surplus (~1.2 mb/d) landing in August, and global inventories built 225 mb from January to a four-year-high 7.9 bn bbl. The WTI curve has consequently sat in contango for much of 2026, which matters mechanically for the short leg specifically: USO holds front-month WTI futures and pays that roll cost every month, whereas SLV holds allocated bullion with no roll at all -- so the spread earns the scarcity/roll differential without any directional forecast on either leg. This is a static structural risk-premium bet, not mean reversion: it is deliberately NOT the pair_zscore shape, because a persistent supply deficit on one side and a persistent glut on the other imply drift, not a spread that returns to its mean. The real risk being borne, stated plainly: silver's industrial demand is pro-cyclical, so a growth shock hits the long leg while a supply disruption (OPEC+ reversing, Gulf outage) hits the short leg -- both legs can lose together, and the 2026 glut is a policy choice OPEC+ can unmake. Distinct from the already-proposed rp_static_spread_carry_SLV_GLD_a (silver against a monetary metal, no energy leg) and rp_static_spread_carry_USO_DBC_a (crude against a broad diversified basket, no metals-scarcity claim); neither is this the sign-flip of any existing pipeline row. Chosen over a broad-basket commodity trend leg because the 2026 picture is explicitly divergent by sub-complex -- energy in glut, agriculture amply supplied, metals tight -- so the aggregate index averages the very dispersion this spread is trying to hold. Primitive tally note (2026-08-12): static_spread_carry is the most-proposed primitive at 9 uses against 7 for each of the other five; taken deliberately anyway, since an always-on relative physical-supply bet is the only shape in the current vocabulary that expresses this mechanism (asset_class_trend_hedge mechanically rejects two commodity legs, and pair_zscore asserts the opposite dynamics).

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_SPY_DBC_252_63
rationale: The mechanism this pair is built on is a regime change in WHICH asset offsets equity risk, and that change is documented rather than assumed. The San Francisco Fed's August 2026 Economic Letter 'Financial Markets, Oil Prices, and Supply-Side Risks' reads the stock-bond correlation as a live indicator of whether supply or demand shocks dominate the risks to activity, and finds it has flipped -- after two decades in which the primary risks were demand-side (zero lower bound, secular stagnation), market pricing now points to elevated oil prices and inflation as the prominent source of risk, with the stock-oil correlation shifting in agreement. The IMF made the portfolio consequence explicit in February 2026: stock-bond diversification offers less protection from selloffs, because the same inflation impulse that pushes bond yields up is what is hurting equities -- so duration, the offset a SPY/TLT or SPY/IEF construction relies on, is exactly the leg that stops working in this regime. The specific offsetting mechanism claimed here is the regime-conditional sign flip in the equity/commodity relationship, not an observed low correlation: measured across 1970-2026 the commodity-equity correlation is +0.27 with CPI below 2%, +0.02 at 2-4%, and -0.06 above 4%, and the event evidence matches the sign story -- commodities fell WITH stocks in the demand shocks of 2008 and 2020 but rose ~18% against an ~18% S&P decline in the 2022 supply shock. A supply/inflation impulse therefore drives the two legs' trailing-return signs in OPPOSITE directions by construction (input costs up: commodity trend positive, equity margins and multiples compressed: equity trend negative), while a demand impulse drives them the same way -- which is precisely why this is a hedge whose value is state-contingent on the regime the SF Fed letter says we are currently in, and equally why it can lose on both legs in a demand shock. The horizon asymmetry is the mechanism, not a fitted parameter: the equity leg gets the canonical 12-month (252d) time-series-momentum horizon because equity trend regimes turn on a slow clock, while the commodity leg gets one quarter (63d) because a supply shock transmits to commodity prices in weeks -- a 252d commodity leg would still be reading the pre-shock regime at exactly the moment the hedge is supposed to pay. Weekly rebalance for the same reason: at monthly the 63d leg can sit up to 21 trading days stale through the impulse it exists to catch. Honest statement of what is being borne: this is two trend legs, and every trend strategy tested in this lab is DEAD -- the claim is not that either leg has standalone edge but that their shock-response signs are opposed in a supply-driven regime, which is the compositional claim this primitive exists to test and which gate 2's diversifier clause is deliberately skeptical of. Distinct from the already-proposed rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_SPY_GLD_252_252 (gold is a monetary/real-rate leg, not a broad input-cost basket, and at 252/252 it makes no horizon-asymmetry claim), rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_SPY_IEF_252_63 (the duration offset this proposal argues has structurally stopped working), and rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_DBC_252_60 / rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_VNQ_DBC_189_63 (neither has an equity leg, so neither expresses the equity-vs-input-cost sign flip). Primitive tally note (2026-08-12): asset_class_trend_hedge is at 7 uses, tied for least-used with four others against static_spread_carry's 10, so this is not a default reach for the crowded shape. Note the mechanical guard this must still clear and may well fail: the calibration-window (2007-2017) leg-correlation cap. That window is, by the SF Fed letter's own account, the demand-shock era in which these two legs moved together -- so a rejection there would be the guard correctly refusing to take a regime claim on faith from out-of-window reasoning, and is an acceptable outcome for this proposal.
