name: rp_pair_zscore_VNQ_IEF_120_2p0_4p0
rationale: Structural, not a track-record claim -- I assert nothing about how VNQ, IEF, listed real estate or any live strategy has recently performed. THE MECHANISM: a mean-reversion primitive needs a TETHER between its two legs and an identifiable economic agent who closes the gap; most UNIVERSE pairs have the first at best. This one has both, and both are measured in primary data rather than asserted. (1) THE TETHER IS THE DISCOUNT RATE. A listed REIT is a claim on property cash flows discounted at the 10-year Treasury yield plus a cap-rate spread, and IEF is a direct instrument on that same 10-year point. Nareit's own Q1 2026 data confirms the linkage is live rather than notional: the REIT IMPLIED cap rate is 5.89%, 169bp above the 10-year Treasury, and Nareit states explicitly that the REIT implied cap rate 'has reacted meaningfully to changes in the 10-year Treasury yield' while the private NCREIF ODCE APPRAISAL cap rate (4.44%, only 24bp over the 10-year) has not, having sat essentially unmoved at its year-end-2021 level for three years. So the log spread log(VNQ)-log(IEF) is, structurally, the listed property risk premium: the two legs share one dominant driver, and what is left over is the cap-rate spread. (2) THE AGENT WHO CLOSES THE GAP IS A TAKE-PRIVATE BUYER, not an abstract 'it should revert'. US REITs above $200M market cap closed Q1 2026 at a median 19.3% discount to consensus NAV; S&P Global counts four US REIT M&A deals totalling $16.77bn announced through 2026-04-15, three of them privatizations of public equity REITs, and ALL FOUR targeted companies trading at a significant discount to NAV, at 20-40% premiums to the unaffected share price. That is a real, capitalized bid that appears when listed pricing detaches from the private mark -- the closest thing this UNIVERSE offers to a mechanical restoring force behind a relative-value spread. THE SINGLE BIGGEST WEAKNESS, STATED FIRST RATHER THAN BURIED: the restoring force runs on a MULTI-QUARTER clock and this primitive cannot wait for it. Nareit puts the current public-private valuation divergence at 17 quarters and still open; an M&A process takes quarters to announce and close. pair_zscore normalizes against a trailing window capped at 120 trading days (~6 months), so what is actually under test is short-horizon reversion around a ROLLING mean, NOT convergence of the structural gap itself -- and a 17-quarter-old gap is precisely the kind that a rolling mean absorbs into its own baseline instead of trading against. If the only real reversion here lives at a horizon longer than the primitive can see, this should and will die on gate 1, and that is the honest prior going in. SECOND WEAKNESS: VNQ is equity and IEF is not, so the spread carries an unhedged equity-beta residual that no 1:1 log spread removes (this primitive fits no hedge ratio, unlike family N's regressed beta). A broad equity drawdown widens the spread with no REIT-specific dislocation behind it, and March 2020 -- listed REITs sold off hard while Treasuries rallied -- is the worst single realization available in the OOS window. It is exactly the realization that should kill this if the spread is really a levered equity bet wearing a relative-value label. THIRD, AGAINST MY OWN THESIS: the dislocation on offer has been SHRINKING, not widening -- the same median NAV discount was 8.7% by mid-2026 against 19.3% at Q1. A smaller gap means less for the mechanism to close, which is a reason to expect failure, not a caveat appended to a bullish case. I propose it anyway because waiting for a wider gap would be timing, and pre-registration is what stops that from being decided after the fact. DISTINCT FROM WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: no graveyard.csv row uses VNQ/IEF, and family N's six pre-registered cointegration pairs (GLD/SLV, TLT/IEF, EFA/EEM, SPY/QQQ, USO/DBC, LQD/HYG) do not include it -- so unlike most remaining pair candidates in this UNIVERSE, this one is not contraindicated by an already-failed ADF test. rp_static_spread_carry_VNQ_IEF_a touches the same two tickers under a DIFFERENT primitive and a different hypothesis -- a persistent premium in the spread's DRIFT versus reversion around its mean -- with its own name and its own separate verdict, the same distinction this ledger already drew between rp_static_spread_carry_LQD_IEF_a and rp_pair_zscore_LQD_IEF_120_2p0_4p0; neither borrows the other's evidence. PARAMETER CHOICES, each tied to the mechanism rather than tuned: z_window=120 is the LONGEST window the primitive offers, chosen because the dislocation is driven by quarterly NAV marks and multi-quarter deal processes -- a shorter window would normalize away the very deviation being traded. z_entry=2.0 / z_stop=4.0 are this lab's OWN already-pre-registered pair thresholds (family N, from Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst 2006's canonical 2-sigma construction), deliberately reused rather than searched over. freq=W because the signal's state changes on a ~6-month normalization against a multi-quarter mechanism: rebalancing daily would pay turnover the hypothesis never earns, and gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched, so the candidate is charged for exactly that. BREADTH: pair_zscore is tied for least-proposed in this ledger (7 of 46 prior rows, against static_spread_carry's 10), and this is its first use of the real_estate asset class.

S&P Global Market Intelligence, 'US REIT M&A activity ramp-up extends into early months of 2026' (2026-04, spglobal.com) -- four US REIT M&A deals totalling $16.77bn announced through 2026-04-15, three of them privatizations of public equity REITs, all four targets trading at a significant discount to NAV; median NAV discount for US REITs above $200M market cap 19.3% at Q1 2026, narrowing to 8.7% by mid-2026; recent take-privates struck at 20-40% premiums to unaffected share prices. Family N's pre-registered pairs and Engle-Granger results (STRATEGIES.md) confirm VNQ/IEF is not among the six pairs already ADF-tested and dropped. name: rp_single_asset_trend_DBC_126
rationale: The broad commodity complex is currently in a deep low-inventory state, which is the precondition the theory of storage says makes a signed directional position on a commodity index economically different from a coin flip. The 2026 Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz disruption took an estimated ~5.5 mb/d of Middle East crude production offline on average during July 2026 -- more than 5% of global consumption -- and crude and refined-product curves returned to extreme backwardation after fighting resumed 2026-07-08; the Bloomberg Commodity Index's index-weighted implied carry was reported at +13% as of 2026-03-31 against a firmly negative -1.3% median since May 2011, and the broader complex (copper, platinum) is running physical deficits with global stockpiles and spare capacity eroding. Two mechanical consequences follow, neither of which is a claim about any strategy's recent performance: (1) when inventories fall far enough that convenience yield exceeds storage plus financing, curves invert and a long futures position earns a positive roll return instead of paying contango drag; (2) the same depleted buffer stocks are what normally damp a spot shock, so with them gone price moves propagate rather than being absorbed -- i.e. the sign of a trailing return carries more information about the next period in a low-inventory regime than in a well-supplied one. DBC is a futures-holding ETF whose Optimum Yield roll targets backwardated contracts, so both effects land directly in the price series engine.py loads, making this testable with spot ETF closes alone. A 126-day (~6 month) lookback matches the horizon over which inventory cycles resolve and spans the disruption regime that began in late February 2026; monthly rebalancing keeps turnover low for a slow-moving structural state. Distinct from the already-tested rp_single_asset_trend_USO_126 (single front-month WTI, no cross-commodity inventory channel) and from the DBC legs inside rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_DBC_252_60 and _VNQ_DBC_189_63, which use different lookbacks and are only ever held against an offsetting leg. Stated honestly against this lab's own record: every trend primitive tested here is DEAD, and backwardation can collapse back to contango quickly -- the pre-registered claim is narrowly that the inventory/roll channel is a structural reason a broad-commodity trend sign might carry information a pure price-trend does not, and the OOS gate decides.
citation: Mechanism: Gorton, Hayashi & Rouwenhorst (2013), 'The Fundamentals of Commodity Futures Returns', Review of Finance 17(1) -- inventories drive backwardation and the predictability of commodity futures returns (theory of storage, Kaldor/Working). Current conditions: CME Group, 'Implications of WTI Oil Futures In Backwardation Amid the Supply Crunch' and 'How Backwardation Generates Positive Roll Returns in Energy' (cmegroup.com/insights/economic-research/2026/) -- crude and refined-product curves in extreme backwardation since 2026-07-08, positive roll return to a rolled long position; S&P Global Market Intelligence, 'Commodity Price Watch: July 2026' -- ~5.5 mb/d of Middle East production offline on average in July 2026, >5% of global consumption, US-Iran MOU reopening Hormuz transit; Aberdeen Investments, 'Commodities June outlook: An illusion of abundance' (2026-06) -- global stockpiles declining and spare capacity eroding across oil and metals, disruptions absorbed via inventory drawdown; IBKR Campus, 'What does today's commodity market mean for broad allocations?' -- reports BCOM index-weighted implied carry of +13% at 2026-03-31 vs a -1.3% median since May 2011, and describes DBC's Optimum Yield roll methodology.

name: rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_20_4
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- and the honest reading of the mechanism's own literature argues the UNCONDITIONAL version of this trade should fail here, which is why that is stated up front rather than buried. THE MECHANISM. Cross-sectional short-horizon reversal is not a forecast of anything; it is the return to LIQUIDITY PROVISION. When non-informational order flow -- forced rebalancing, hedging demand, an outage-driven scramble for one asset -- displaces an asset's price relative to its peers, whoever takes the other side is paid a premium for absorbing it, and the premium is realised as the displacement decays. Nagel (2012, RFS 25(7)) establishes the two facts this proposal rests on: (a) reversal-strategy returns proxy for the returns to liquidity provision, and (b) that expected return is strongly TIME-VARYING and rises with market-wide volatility, as financially-constrained intermediaries withdraw liquidity supply and the price of supplying it goes up. Crucially, Nagel also finds that reversal formed from COARSE BASKETS (industry portfolios) does NOT earn high returns unconditionally, and only pays in high-volatility states. This lab's UNIVERSE is 15 broad ETFs -- coarser still than industry portfolios -- so the pre-registered expectation here is explicitly the conditional case, not the unconditional one. If the conditional premium is not large enough to survive DSR/CPCV over the full 2018+ OOS window, this dies, and that is the correct outcome. WHY THIS REGIME, NOW. The current setup is a supply-shock/dispersion regime, not a demand-cycle one: crude and refined products have returned to sharp backwardation on physical outages tied to Strait of Hormuz disruption (CME Group, 2026: WTI Jun-2026 at a $20.65 premium to Jun-2027), which is a scarcity-premium displacement concentrated in one asset class rather than a broad repricing. At the same time bond volatility is dormant (MOVE ~74.7) and HY OAS sits in its richest decile (~271-281bp) with the Fed easing -- so realised dispersion ACROSS asset classes is wide while dispersion WITHIN the rates complex is compressed. Multi-asset commentary going into 2026 (Vontobel, Goldman Sachs AM) frames rising cross-asset and cross-country dispersion driven by divergent fiscal policy and supply shocks as the defining feature of the regime. Dispersion is the raw material a cross-sectional rank needs: with near-zero dispersion, top-K and bottom-K are noise. WHY DOLLAR-NEUTRAL MATTERS HERE. Oxford Economics expects the stock-bond correlation to turn positive again in 2026 on supply shocks and activist fiscal policy, which impairs the channel the fair 60/40 benchmark relies on. A long-top-K/short-bottom-K book is dollar-neutral by construction and does not borrow that channel, so gate 3 (correlation to the benchmark) is a claim this shape can actually make. WHY THESE PARAMETERS, AND HOW IT DIFFERS FROM WHAT IS ALREADY IN THE LEDGER. lookback=20 is the FLOOR of the pre-registered range -- the closest this vocabulary gets to the roughly one-month horizon the reversal literature actually studies; anything longer is a valuation claim, not a liquidity-provision one. freq=D is the substantive choice and the first daily rebalance ever proposed for this primitive: the two prior reversal proposals in this ledger (rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_21_3 at M, rp_cross_sectional_rank_reversal_42_2 at W, neither of which has reached an OOS verdict) hold a position for a month or a week while the displacement they are formed on decays in days, so they cannot express this mechanism at all -- a monthly-rebalanced 21-day reversal is a different strategy from a daily-rebalanced 20-day one, not a neighbouring parameter. k=4 (long 4, short 4 of 15) is chosen for breadth: a liquidity premium is small per name, so it needs positions, and k=4 is the widest setting that still leaves a genuine middle of the ranking untraded. Note this is CROSS-SECTIONAL, distinct from the time-series str_reversal_* family (3d-23d) already dead in graveyard.csv, which reverses each asset against its OWN past rather than against its peers.
citation: Nagel, S. (2012), 'Evaporating Liquidity', Review of Financial Studies 25(7), 2005-2039 (https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/25/7/2005/1602153; NBER WP 17653) -- reversal returns as the return to liquidity provision, time-varying and predictable by volatility, and weak unconditionally for coarse baskets. Lehmann, B. (1990), 'Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency', QJE 105(1), for the original short-horizon cross-sectional reversal result. Current-regime facts: CME Group Economic Research (2026), 'Implications of WTI Oil Futures In Backwardation Amid the Supply Crunch' (https://www.cmegroup.com/insights/economic-research/2026/implications-of-wti-oil-futures-in-backwardation-amid-the-supply-crunch.html); Vontobel AM, '2026: Multi Asset Reloaded' and Goldman Sachs AM, 'Market Know-How 3Q 2026', on rising cross-asset/cross-country dispersion; Oxford Economics, 'Stock bond correlation will become positive again in 2026'.

name: rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_IEF_a
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- I assert nothing about how gold, Treasuries or any live strategy has recently performed, and the single strongest piece of evidence I found argues AGAINST this proposal, so it is stated first rather than buried. THE MECHANISM: official-sector reserve substitution. A central bank's FX reserve portfolio is a choice between a small number of substitutable stores of value, and the two largest are US Treasuries and gold. The World Gold Council's 2026 Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey (76 respondents, its largest ever) records that gold overtook US Treasuries by market value at end-2025 -- 27% of global official reserves versus 22% -- that central banks have bought an average of ~1,000t/yr over the past four years against a ~500t/yr average the preceding decade, that 89% expect global gold reserves to rise over the next 12 months, and that 74% expect LOWER US dollar holdings over the next five years. The stated motive has also changed in kind, not just degree: 84% now hold gold as a long-term store of value, while 'historical legacy' fell from 62% to 46% year over year. That is a price-INSENSITIVE, mandate-driven marginal buyer of one asset funded by a stated intent to underweight the other -- the shape static_spread_carry exists to express (an always-on structural risk-premium/flow bet, not a mean-reversion signal and not a trend forecast). WHY THE SHORT LEG IS IEF SPECIFICALLY, AND WHY IT IS NOT A LEVERED GOLD BET. Gold and nominal duration share one dominant driver: the real discount rate. Gold is effectively a zero-coupon perpetual real claim, so falling real yields lift it and lift IEF at the same time. Shorting the nominal-duration leg is therefore not decoration -- it removes the factor both assets already have in common and leaves gold's residual monetary/official-demand component, which is the only part the mechanism above actually speaks to. IEF rather than TLT because reserve portfolios are held for liquidity and are concentrated in the short-to-intermediate Treasury sector; the 20yr+ sector TLT tracks is dominated by pensions, insurers and leveraged accounts, not reserve managers, so IEF is the closest instrument in this UNIVERSE to the maturity bucket the substitution actually happens in. engine.py vol-targets each leg, so this is a relative claim between two vol-scaled sleeves, not an equal-notional bet dominated by gold's ~3x higher realised volatility. THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT AGAINST, FROM A PRIMARY SOURCE. IMF COFER for 2026Q1 shows the US dollar's share of allocated FX reserves ROSE to 57.13% from 56.42% in 2025Q4, with the IMF attributing roughly half of that increase to exchange-rate valuation effects -- and the IMF explicitly notes that gold overtaking Treasuries in 2025 was driven ALMOST ENTIRELY BY GOLD PRICE VALUATION EFFECTS, not by net selling of Treasuries. If the headline 27%-vs-22% crossover is mostly a price artefact of the very asset I am proposing to be long, then the crossover is a CONSEQUENCE of gold's repricing rather than evidence of a forward flow, and this spread is closer to an extrapolation of a past move than to harvesting a premium. That is the honest prior going in. THREE FURTHER WEAKNESSES. (1) MAGNITUDE ASYMMETRY: ~1,000t/yr is on the order of $100bn against a Treasury market measured in tens of trillions -- the flow is large relative to annual gold supply and negligible relative to the short leg's market, so the mechanism is lopsided and only one leg is really being pushed. (2) IT IS PUBLIC: a widely-published survey-documented flow is exactly the kind whose expected excess return should already be discounted into the level; static_spread_carry has no timing element whatsoever, so if the ratio already reflects a decade of this, forward return can be negative even while the flow continues exactly as described. (3) THIS LAB'S OWN RECORD: the one surviving carry-shaped strategy here (delta-neutral crypto funding) pays for bearing an identifiable, nameable tail risk. I cannot name the equivalent risk this spread is compensated for bearing, which makes it a relative-value directional view wearing a carry label -- a reason to expect DEAD, not a caveat appended to a bullish case. Gate 3 is a real hurdle regardless: gold's own 2012-2015 drawdown was roughly -45%, far worse than a 60/40's, and the short-IEF leg does not hedge that. DISTINCT FROM WHAT IS ALREADY IN THIS LEDGER. GLD/IEF appears under no primitive in pipeline_ideas.csv and no graveyard.csv row uses the pair. rp_static_spread_carry_GLD_UUP_a is gold versus the DOLLAR -- an FX-level claim about the currency itself -- whereas this is gold versus USD DURATION ASSETS, a reserve-composition claim with a different short leg and a different mechanism. rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_TLT_GLD_126_189 touches gold and Treasuries under a different primitive (two trend-following legs, no always-on position), at the long-bond maturity the substitution argument above specifically does NOT apply to; neither borrows the other's evidence. PARAMETERS. static_spread_carry has no fitted parameters by construction -- ticker_a=GLD as the accumulated asset, ticker_b=IEF as the diversified-away-from asset, long_leg='a' in the direction the documented flow runs, which is the only assignment the mechanism permits. freq=M because the state variable is a reserve-allocation decision reported and revised quarterly; a faster rebalance would pay turnover the hypothesis never earns, and gate 1's null is duty-cycle-matched so the candidate is charged for exactly that. BREADTH NOTE, STATED PLAINLY: static_spread_carry is the MOST-proposed primitive in this ledger (10 of 49 prior rows, against curve_carry's 7), so this proposal does not help vocabulary coverage. No primitive is heavily under-represented (the spread across all six is 7 to 10), curve_carry's only parameter is a lookback and 21/42/63/84/126/189/252 are already taken, and today's research pointed at an official-sector flow between two specific tickers rather than at the TLT/IEF curve -- so I chose merit over a one-count rebalance, per the stated preference-not-a-rule.
citation: World Gold Council, 'Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey 2026' (gold.org/goldhub/research/central-bank-gold-reserves-survey-2026), and WGC press release 'Central banks set to step up gold buying over the next year' -- 76 respondents (largest in the survey's nine-year history); gold surpassed US Treasuries by market value at end-2025 at 27% of global official reserves vs 22%; central banks bought an average of ~1,000t/yr over the past four years vs a ~500t/yr average the preceding decade; 89% expect global gold reserves to rise over the next 12 months; 74% expect lower US dollar holdings over the next five years; 84% cite long-term store of value as a reason to hold gold, with 'historical legacy' falling from 62% (2025) to 46% (2026). Reported via Kitco News, 'Record 45% of central banks plan to increase gold holdings, WGC survey finds' (2026-06-16). COUNTER-EVIDENCE, weighted deliberately: IMF COFER, 'Currency Composition of Official Foreign Exchange Reserves' data brief (data.imf.org) -- the US dollar share of allocated reserves ROSE to 57.13% in 2026Q1 from 56.42% in 2025Q4, with roughly half the increase attributable to exchange-rate valuation effects, and the IMF states that gold surpassing US Treasuries as a share of official reserves in 2025 was driven almost entirely by gold PRICE valuation effects and is not reflected in a declining COFER dollar share (COFER methodology revised from 2025Q3, unallocated reserves eliminated with revisions back to 2000Q1). Additional 2026 volume context: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends Q2 2026 and CME Group, 'Precious Metals Outlook 2026' -- central bank purchases running at roughly 850t projected for 2026, with sustained multi-month official-sector accumulation. Mechanism (real-rate factor shared by gold and nominal duration, motivating the IEF short leg rather than an outright gold position): standard gold-as-zero-coupon-real-asset framing, e.g. Barro & Misra (2016), 'Gold Returns', Economic Journal 126(594).

name: rp_pair_zscore_HYG_IEF_120_1p75_5p0
rationale: HYG/IEF is the tradable form of the high-yield option-adjusted spread: HY OAS is quoted over Treasuries, so the HYG-vs-IEF log-spread proxies the credit risk premium itself more directly than HYG/LQD, which nets two credit instruments against each other. That premium is currently compressed to a structural extreme -- HY OAS ~271-281bp in early August 2026, the richest decile of its own history against a long-run median near 450bp, with IG at 81bp and bond volatility dormant (MOVE 74.7). This is a claim about the LEVEL of compensation for default risk, not about what has recently performed. pair_zscore is the conditional expression of it: flat near the mean, taking risk only when the spread is statistically extreme, unlike an always-on static_spread_carry which cannot express 'this premium is mispriced right now'. z_window=120 (top of range, ~6 months) because credit cycles mean-revert far more slowly than equity pairs and a short window would define 'unusual' against weeks of noise. z_entry=1.75 rather than higher because HY spread distributions are strongly right-skewed -- they spike wide and grind tight -- so the compressed side rarely reaches high z and a 2.0+ entry would leave a regime like today's untradeable. z_stop=5.0 for the same skew: HY OAS reached multiples of current levels in 2008 and 2020, so a tight stop exits at the crisis extreme rather than on genuine reversion failure. Identified decompression catalysts: energy is ~10% of the HY index with Brent near $91 on Middle East supply risk, and September brings the heaviest post-summer issuance calendar at minimal concessions. Prior is that this dies like everything else here (pairs/cointegration is already DEAD across six pre-registered pairs); the credit-premium-level pair has not been tested against the gates in this form.

name: rp_asset_class_trend_hedge_QQQ_USO_200_40
rationale: STRUCTURAL, NOT A TRACK-RECORD CLAIM -- nothing below asserts that trend-following, commodities, tech or any live strategy has recently performed well; every input is a statement about the current transmission structure between two shock channels. THE MECHANISM, NAMED SPECIFICALLY (required by this primitive, which will not accept 'these two happen to be uncorrelated'): the QQQ leg and the USO leg sit on opposite ends of ONE causal chain -- crude oil is the principal transmitter of inflation shocks into the 10-year real yield, and the 10-year real yield is the dominant valuation variable for the longest-duration equity claim in this UNIVERSE. QQQ's cash flows are the most distant of any UNIVERSE equity ETF, so its multiple is disproportionately a discounted-value function of the real rate; an energy-led inflation impulse raises breakevens and term premium, lifts the real discount rate, and de-rates exactly that multiple, while the same impulse is what a crude trend leg goes long into. Run the chain the other way and it still holds: a disinflationary crude decline lowers the real discount rate and re-rates QQQ upward while the crude trend leg is short. That is a directional, checkable transmission claim -- not a correlation search. WHY THE HEDGE LEG IS A COMMODITY AND NOT DURATION, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF PICKING THIS PAIR NOW. The textbook offset for an equity-duration shock is nominal duration (TLT/IEF), and that offset is structurally impaired in the current regime: Oxford Economics' 2026 work argues the stock-bond correlation returns to POSITIVE territory in 2026 and that the pre-Covid regime of weakly pro-cyclical inflation does not sustainably return, with continued supply shocks, geopolitical risk and more activist fiscal policy pushing term premia higher. When the correlation is positive, a rates leg does not offset an equity-duration shock -- it SHARES it, because both legs are then being driven by the same inflation/term-premium factor. So the hedge for long-duration equity has to come from the asset class that is the SOURCE of that factor rather than another victim of it. This is also why the pair is admissible under the primitive's asset-class rule for a real reason and not merely a bookkeeping one: QQQ resolves to equity, USO to commodity. WHY USO RATHER THAN DBC. DBC is a diversified basket whose energy exposure is diluted by metals and agriculture and whose optimised roll rule deliberately blunts the front of the curve; the inflation-transmission channel argued above is specifically CRUDE, so the pure front-month WTI instrument is the sharper expression of the stated mechanism, not a broader-is-better diversifier claim. A SECONDARY, PARTIAL AND DELIBERATELY NOT OVERSOLD POINT ON THE USO LEG. USO holds and rolls front-month WTI, so its price series -- which is what engine.load_prices() sees -- mechanically embeds roll yield. The WTI curve is currently backwardated (CME Group's 2026 'Implications of WTI Oil Futures In Backwardation Amid the Supply Crunch'; a gently backwardated Brent strip running from roughly USD 79/bbl for Oct-2026 down toward USD 69-70/bbl by 2029 as of early August 2026), which means a LONG USO position is roll-yield-supported while held. I am not counting this as carry, because this primitive takes both signs via sign(): the same structure that pays the long side charges the short side symmetrically. It is a reason the long half of the leg is cheaper to hold, not an edge.
